facts.text: Shau Kei Wan was once a small fishing village called Saukaywan, meaning 'bay of the rope measure' in Cantonese.
The Tam Kung Temple, built in 1905 during the Guangxu era, has stood for more than a century and houses a century‑old bell and wall paintings.
The Hong Kong Museum of Coastal Defence, converted from the Old Lei Yue Mun Fort, preserves 400 exhibits that trace more than six hundred years of defence history.
Shau Kei Wan Road, the main artery, was once part of a north‑coast route linking Causeway Bay to Shau Kei Wan via North Point and Quarry Bay.
Shau Kei Wan Main Street East hosts more than 60 restaurants and a century‑old banyan tree, making it a long‑standing food hub.
The area’s name derives from its sieve‑like gulf contour, a detail noted by early developers who named it Shau Kei Wan.
